name: bench-charming

purpose.why: Rebuilt on Evan's request (2026-10-22) to replace the Ranch tile's original model with a crafted one, keeping its game role.
purpose.audience: children building and playing in a miniature ranch

brief.prompt: a whimsical storybook version of a simple rustic wooden garden bench, a thick plank seat on sturdy splayed legs with a stretcher, chunky rounded toy-like proportions, a playful little tilt

concept.tool: Midjourney web app (midjourney.com/imagine), driven in Evan's signed-in Chrome by Claude through the Claude in Chrome extension, one job at a time, text prompts only (no image reference)

hero.prompt: a whimsical storybook version of a simple rustic wooden garden bench, a thick plank seat on sturdy splayed legs with a stretcher, chunky rounded toy-like proportions, a playful little tilt, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 1:1
hero.pick_reason: chunky plank seat on splayed legs with stretcher, whole bench with margin

turnaround.prompt: orthographic turnaround sheet, front view, side view, back view, evenly spaced, same scale, a whimsical storybook version of a simple rustic wooden garden bench, a thick plank seat on sturdy splayed legs with a stretcher, chunky rounded toy-like proportions, a playful little tilt, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 16:9
turnaround.pick_reason: long side, end view and three-quarter of one bench in a single row, largest views

construction.by: modeler agent, directed by the art director (Claude)

rounds.change: Charming rebuild from the normal bench: one pillow-edged 0.15 m slab with sag, kicked-up ends and a tilt; four round bulging log legs; wobbly round stretcher, round end rails, fat pegs; caps and diagonal braces dropped (not in the hero). Sheet front view scored 0.126 and dropped.
Thicker 0.17 m slab, much smaller end kick (25 to 10 mm), fatter legs (r 0.084-0.092 m), seat top 0.54 m; hero camera recalibrated (kept -38/12).
Swept slab thickness, height, splay, lean, leg spacing and depth; slab to 0.14 m (biggest gain), others kept. Colours deepened to the hero's red-brown (Plank_Walnut 150,76,38; Timber_Dark 84,42,22).
Tried a higher, thinner stretcher (0.80, reverted) and fatter legs (no gain); per-leg random lean raised to 4 deg for more wonk (neutral at low res). Final 768 px / 48 sample render.

what_was_done: Copied the finished normal bench (build.py, make_views.py, hero_check.py, run.sh) and reshaped it: same origin (footprint centre on the ground), long side facing -Y, same three objects (seat, legs, frame), same two materials and roles (Plank_Walnut, Timber_Dark), no states (a garden prop). Footprint 1.61 x 0.61 m (ratio 2.62 against the normal 2.51), seat top 0.54 m.

The hero wins and is the only target. views/hero.png is the MJ hero keyed by hue: backdrop G/R ~0.89, the soft cast shadow G/R ~0.80, the wood 0.49-0.66, so G/R < 0.74 keeps the bench and drops the shadow; the openings between seat, legs and stretcher stay open. The turnaround sheet drew a taller, lighter bench with square-sawn legs and stretchers plus end rails at mid height, and its cuts are 3/4 views with big cast shadows (the long-side cut scored 0.13, mostly shadow and sky), so all three sheet views are dropped.

hero_check.py from the normal bench, unchanged: 38 deg off the front towards -X, 12 deg up, 85 mm perspective. A recalibration over the yaw/elevation grid put -38/12 in the top group again, so it was kept.

Plank_Walnut: one chubby 1.60 x 0.44 x 0.14 m slab instead of two planks, with pillow edges (55 mm, 3-segment bevel), a 10 mm sag in the middle and the ends kicked up 10 mm, the ends flaring 6 % wider, edge vertices nudged up to 12 mm for a hand-carved wobble, and the whole slab tipped 1.2 deg (right end up) and 1 deg back for a playful tilt.

Plank_Walnut: four fat round 10-sided logs (radius 84 mm at the top, 92 mm bulging at the middle, 90 mm at the foot) with rounded-in feet cut flat on the ground, splayed from y = +-0.10 under the seat to +-0.22 at the ground and leaning 6 cm outward along X, each with its own random extra lean of up to 4 deg so the bench looks hand-made and a little wonky. Each leg top is set into the tilted seat's underside.

Timber_Dark: a thin round stretcher at 0.19 m that wobbles gently along its length and swells at its fat tenons poking 0.12 m past each end, a round end rail between each leg pair, and a fat bevelled peg through each tenon.
3 objects, one material each, 1160 triangles (budget 2k). Installed with to_game.py to garden-assets-charming/GF-194.glb.
construction.creative_additions: A playful tilt of the seat, each leg leaning at its own angle, the plank ends flaring wider, and fat pegged tenons on a gently wobbling stretcher.

geometry.up: Z (Blender source); Y in GLB and game
geometry.origin: centre of the footprint, on the ground

good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.839 at the final 768 px / 48 sample render (0.857 at 384 px / 16 samples).
Reads as the same bench as the normal one (thick seat, splayed leg pairs, dark stretcher with pegged tenons) but softer and toy-like: round chubby legs, pillowy slab, a little tilt and wonk.
Same footprint proportions, origin, orientation and materials as the normal bench, so it drops in place.
off: The hero's seat looks a touch thicker than 0.14 m; thicker slabs scored lower (0.811 at 0.17 m) because the hero camera sits low, so 0.14 m with pillowy edges is the compromise.
The hero's stretcher sits a little higher up the legs and is very thin and rough; raising it to 0.23 m scored lower (0.80), so it stays at 0.19 m.
The hero's cast shadow is keyed out by hue; a few shadowed under-leg pixels may be lost at the feet.
No wood grain, knots or cracks: flat colours only, per the game rules. Turnaround sheet not scored (dropped, see Views).

rights: Original work for Abbie's World. Concept art generated on Evan's Midjourney account; geometry generated procedurally, no third-party meshes or textures.
